about: Ad Shield's own scriptlet rules (MIT). Each rule: hosts (each covers its subdomains) and scriptlets ([name, ...string args]) from src/scriptlets/lib.js. Built into build/scriptlets-main.js by tools/build.py; shipped in the package, never downloaded. Object paths and URL patterns: docs/research-v2.md section B. The YouTube anti-adblock dialog is closed by youtube-enforcement-dismiss, not hidden by CSS (hiding kept its scroll lock and pauses).

rules.about: Ad data removed before the player sees it, with as few hooks as possible (docs/DESIGN-v2.md, YouTube): the page-embedded player response and initial data (one-time setter traps; feed, search and Shorts ad items are pruned only here, later feed pages are left to rules/cosmetic/youtube.css), the player ad keys and a top-level Shorts entries list's isAd items in every JSON.parse / Response.json (plain key lookups after an indexOf needle check), and the youtubei player, get_watch, playlist, resolve_url and Shorts sequence fetch / XHR responses (player keys, the resolve_url prefetch playerResponse at endpoint.watchEndpoint.unserializedPrefetchData, and the Shorts isAd entries). Plus the 17 s "fake buffering" wait of flagged accounts (a native-code callback scheduled with setTimeout 17000) cut to 17 ms (research B section 1). Anti-bypass (uBO quick-fixes.txt: trusted-prevent-dom-bypass, Node.prototype.appendChild, fetch / Request; rmnt, script, 'window,"fetch"'): an iframe appended with appendChild gets this window's (wrapped) fetch and Request, so a clean pair taken from a fresh frame still passes through the pruning and body edits, and inline scripts containing window,"fetch" are removed before they run (until DOMContentLoaded). The player's onAbnormalityDetected event (published on an ad context in the SABR stream for a response without a pre-roll, an untrusted Skip click, an ad finished too fast; the main app's listener stops the video and shows the enforcement message) is never delivered: youtube-drop-player-event drops subscriptions to it on the player element, found when the player copies its API onto it (getApiInterface accessor on HTMLElement.prototype; base.js / kevlar_base read 2026-11-22). uBO neuters the same listener through a Promise.prototype.then proxy; we do not hook Promise.prototype.then or Function.prototype.toString (a hook on every then() cost frames) and change no ytcfg flags (uBO dropped web_streaming_watch). Also uBO's "oaeb" tag edit (params oAEBogYBLg, plus #reloadxhr appended to playbackContext.contentPlaybackContext.referer; uAssets filters/quick-fixes.txt, ef0ac51 2026-11-02, dcf5811 2026-11-14 added oaeb, 1fbf62c 2026-11-17) on the two requests that fetch a player response: the youtubei /player request body (only requests with attestationRequest, client WEB) and the playerRequest of the get_watch request that in-page navigation sends (client WEB), by edit-request-body inside the fetch / XHR send wrappers (gzip Request bodies gunzipped and re-gzipped), where uBO uses a JSON.stringify hook. A direct watch-page load takes its player response from the HTML, so rules/youtube.json adds pp=oAEBogYBLg to www.youtube.com/watch page loads (DNR redirect). Why: for a video with a pre-roll YouTube's SABR stream answers with an ad context, a snackbar message and a backoff of 4-9 s (measured 2026-11-20, docs/DESIGN-v2.md); a client that plays the ad hides it behind the ad, a client without ad data shows a black player for that long. With oAEBogYBLg the response has no ad keys and no backoff (also without the extension). Not uBO's "channel" tag (clientScreen CHANNEL: UNPLAYABLE, answer/3037019, measured 2026-11-19) and not "yahi" (params YAHI: the same backoff, measured 2026-11-20). No userAgent tag or tag rotation. Blocked-playback screen ("Ad blockers violate YouTube's Terms of Service" in place of the player; measured 2026-11-22 in Chrome): on a direct watch-page load the HTML's embedded ytInitialPlayerResponse arrives with playabilityStatus OK; YouTube's main app (kevlar_base yje / kHz / Kgb, i4Q.handleResponse, read 2026-11-22) checks it against responseContext.mainAppWebResponseContext.trackingParam (an obfuscated list of path / value pairs) and, for a marked session, about 1.4 s after navigation start replaces playabilityStatus with an ERROR copy (errorScreen.enforcementMessageViewModel, built by Kgb from auxiliaryUi.messageRenderers.bkaEnforcementMessageViewModel with a ..._PLAYER displayType, or errorScreen.playerErrorMessageRenderer with subreason 282054944, kHz) and sets videoDetails to undefined. It does so on an untouched response too, so it is not caused by our pruning. youtube-playability-recover guards every OK response stored in window.ytInitialPlayerResponse or window.ytplayer.bootstrapPlayerResponse (ytplayer may be created later) from document start: accessors on its playabilityStatus and videoDetails ignore exactly that swap (and the videoDetails = undefined that follows it); every other write, such as a different ERROR or a fresh OK object, goes through. The trap chains with the prune-on-assign accessor above (which runs first) and guards the object that accessor stores, the one the page and the player read. The main app does the same to the player responses of in-page navigation (get_watch items' playerResponse, /player; seen live 2026-11-22 as "Something went wrong ... 282054944"), so the same guard is applied to every OK object a JSON.parse (text containing "playabilityStatus") or Response.json returns: the object, its array items, their playerResponse and the resolve_url prefetch playerResponse (key lookups only, after json-prune*). Measured: 3 test videos played 2.5 s, 6.1 s and 6.2 s after navigation start with no block screen (before: block screen shown, playing at about 8.7 s). The fallback, when the response the player uses is still enforced (playabilityStatus ERROR / UNPLAYABLE with errorScreen.enforcementMessageViewModel, errorScreen.playerErrorMessageRenderer with subreason 282054944, or auxiliaryUi.messageRenderers.bkaEnforcementMessageViewModel): ask the player for the video again with #movie_player.loadVideoById(v, t) (uBO's reload-on-UNPLAYABLE idea), at most 3 times per video; it polls the player's getPlayerResponse() every 0.1 s from document start (and again from DOMContentLoaded, yt-navigate-finish and yt-player-updated, for in-page navigation), for at most 20 s after the start or the last reload, and keeps polling after an OK response until the player plays (state 1), because the swap comes after the first OK. It calls loadVideoById only once the page has loaded (readyState complete) or the player has reported onStateChange 5 cued / -1 unstarted (a call while the page is still loading was swallowed), the player is cued, unstarted or buffering (3) now with the enforced response (measured 2026-11-23: a player left on the 282054944 screen sat in state 3 after the load event and was never reloaded) and the enforced response has been seen for 0.3 s; a reload that leaves the same response in place for 3 s while the player is still cued counts as a failed try. Only once the reloaded response for that video is OK does it hide the stale yt-playability-error-supported-renderers, clear player-unavailable on ytd-watch-flexy (YouTube leaves both after a successful reload, measured 2026-11-22) and unhide the player, again 1 s and 3 s later; both are given back on yt-navigate-start. Other playability errors (private, age gate, region) are never touched. auxiliaryUi.messageRenderers.bkaEnforcementMessageViewModel (and playerResponse.auxiliaryUi.messageRenderers.bkaEnforcementMessageViewModel) is pruned with the ad keys by prune-on-assign and json-prune*, as in the measured build; the fallback's enforcement test still also detects errorScreen.enforcementMessageViewModel (the kHz playerErrorMessageRenderer path is the common one).

rules.about: m.youtube.com only (as uBO and AdGuard): ad items (adSlotRenderer) removed from the itemSectionRenderer.contents lists of the youtubei get_watch fetch response, the watch page's list below the player. The body is parsed only when it contains the word adSlotRenderer.

Fallbacks: for ads that still play (e.g. server-side inserted) mute, jump to the end of the ad, unmute afterwards (research B recipe 11; the Skip button is not clicked: the player answers an untrusted click with onAbnormalityDetected instead of skipping); and close YouTube's anti-adblock dialog properly (close() releases its scroll lock and backdrop) and resume a video it paused without the viewer while it is open or just closed (B.3); no repeated seeks within one ad and none in ads over 90 s (stitched streams); pauses from media keys, headphones or picture-in-picture (media session actions) are left alone.
